title: 50 Articles a Day, Moderated in 8 Seconds — From My Phone | vitalii.no
description:
How a single Telegram message that rewrites itself replaced hours of manual moderation with four taps.

Every day 50 or more articles arrived from 6 Telegram channels and a set of RSS feeds. Each one needed the same three decisions made by hand: which image to use, which language to publish in, and which platform it goes to. Doing that in a browser meant hours per batch, and it could only happen at a desk.

A single telegram-webhook Supabase Edge Function, written in Deno, is now the central callback handler for every inline button in the flow. One chat message edits itself in place: it shows the image choice, then rewrites itself into the language choice, then into the platform choice, all in the same bubble. Nothing new is opened and nothing is typed. Telegram caps callback data at 64 bytes, which forced a compact action_prefix_${newsId} pattern where the prefix must stay under 28 characters because a UUID already takes 36. That constraint turned out to be a feature: it keeps every callback unambiguous and stateless. Video posts skip the image step entirely and go straight to the publish buttons.

Average handling time per article fell from hours to 8 seconds and 4 taps, done from a phone, anywhere.
